name: Cefadroxil
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Over 90% of cefadroxil is excreted unchanged in urine within 24 hours. The US label treats creatinine clearance (CrCl) above 50 mL/min/1.73 m2 as normal; below that it gives a 1 g first dose and then 500 mg every 12, 24 or 36 hours as kidney function falls. About 63% of a dose was removed in a 6- to 8-hour hemodialysis.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl in mL/min/1.73 m2; bands at 50, 25 and 10. The mL/min/1.73 m2 unit is the label's own convention and is kept verbatim.

bands.recommendation: CrCl 51–59: usual dose. CrCl 30–50 (label row 25–50): Initial dose 1,000 mg, then 500 mg every 12 hours (label).
CrCl 25–29: Initial dose 1,000 mg, then 500 mg every 12 hours. CrCl 15–24 (label row 10–25): Initial dose 1,000 mg, then 500 mg every 24 hours (label).
CrCl 10–14: Initial dose 1,000 mg, then 500 mg every 24 hours. CrCl 0–10: Initial dose 1,000 mg, then 500 mg every 36 hours (label).

hd.text: No hemodialysis dosing in label. A 6- to 8-hour session removed about 63% of a 1 g dose in anuric patients (label). Specialist input.
hd.short: No label dose; 63% removed by HD

pd.text: No peritoneal dialysis dosing in label. Specialist input.

crrt.text: Not in label; the cited CRRT review (Li 2020) gives no regimen for this drug. Specialist input.
crrt.short: No CRRT data in cited sources

dialyzable: Yes: about 63% of a 1 g dose removed during a 6- to 8-hour hemodialysis (label).
monitoring: CrCl for dose; kidney function tests when indicated (label); diarrhea (CDAD).

pediatric.usual_dose: Urinary tract infections: 30 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours; pharyngitis, tonsillitis, impetigo: 30 mg/kg/day as one or two doses (label).

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney dosing in label (the CrCl table is for adults). Specialist input.
